title: Numerical marked-ideal resolution data and coefficient recursion
statement:
Using the existing stalk ideals of [def-trf-marked-ideal-order], for the marked inputs and histories of [def-trf-marked-ideal-data], let the common numerical alphabet be the ordered tagged sum of $\mathbf Q$, $\mathbf N$ and the lexicographic monomial tuples $(-p,q,A)$ with an additional largest terminal symbol $\infty$. Words are finite lists of entries, ordered lexicographically with the empty continuation smallest. A simultaneous value family assigns a word to every cosupport point of every finite history. Its maximum locus is the entire greatest-value locus. A maximum step blows up exactly this locus, when nonempty. The admissible histories for a family are generated by initial histories, maximum steps, empty-center stages and smooth pullbacks.

A coefficient-recursion certificate for a tail is either a zero-stalk ideal with word $(\infty)$, a monomial ideal $\prod_i I_{E_i}^{a_i}$ with word $(0,\Gamma)$, or a positive pair $(\mu,s)$ followed by a certificate on a smooth hypersurface of strictly smaller local support dimension. Here $\mu=a/b$ is the exact order of the residual after factoring the maximal boundary monomial, and $s$ counts the components through the point born by a recorded earlier cut. The companion is $(R,a)$ if $a\ge b$, and $(R^{b-a}+M^a,a(b-a))$ otherwise, where $I=MR$; augment it by the $d$th powers of the old boundary equations, retain only the new boundary, and restrict the coefficient ideal $\sum_{j<d}(D_{E_{new}}^j J)^{d!/(d-j)}$ with mark $d!$ to a logarithmic maximal-contact hypersurface. The restriction is the actual induced local-ring map. Birth stages of the retained boundary are inherited. For a monomial terminal, among subsets through the point whose exponent sum reaches the mark choose minimal cardinality $p$, then maximal normalized sum $q$, then maximal ordered index tuple $A$; put $\Gamma=(-p,q,A)$.

A numerical-resolution datum is one such value family with: finite image and upper semicontinuity on each admissible cosupport; leading entry 1 for maximal-order inputs; a certificate for the remaining tail; existence of a full-maximum-center extension and strict decrease of every surviving value below the old maximum; unchanged values away from the center; equality under smooth history pullback, with no relative-dimension restriction; equality of tails under test-equivalent identified histories with equal stalk Krull dimension at the corresponding cosupport points; termination of its maximum-center process and absence of an infinite fixed-prefix tail. A finite patched presentation consists of local histories on a finite open cover of an ambient rational scheme, with smooth open restrictions on their overlaps and test-equivalent overlap histories with equal stalk Krull dimension at every pair of corresponding cosupport points. Taking the maximum over their union gives a synchronized step, with empty centers on patches missing that maximum. The datum requires existence of these synchronized steps, gluing of their actual center ideals to a smooth global center, strict decrease of the union maximum and termination of this synchronized process. No well-foundedness of the word order is assumed.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, pp.93--94; BMT arXiv:0905.3580, Remark 5.1 and sections 5.3--5.4, pp.9--11; explicit alphabet, monomial subset invariant and fixed-prefix termination from lem-trf-marked-ideal-numerical-resolution-engine proof steps 1--10.
